sun.upright:
Of all the Suns to draw the Five of Cups, Aries is the least practised at standing still over a loss. You're built to go at things, and a defeat usually gets answered by starting something else before lunch. The odd part is that this is your own planet's card. Mars rules Aries and Scorpio both, and the card is Mars in the opening slice of Scorpio, so it's the same drive that gets you up in the morning, stopped dead and made to feel something it can't hit.

Aries and Scorpio sit five signs apart, a quincunx, and apart from sharing a ruler they have nothing in common. They're fire and water too, the awkward pair of elements. So grief doesn't come to you as sadness. It comes as heat, a restlessness looking for a target, and to be honest you'd rather be angry than sad, because angry has something to do. Nothing here can be fought, though. The chance has gone, or the person has, and Mars without an opponent turns on the nearest thing, usually you, replaying how fast you should have moved.

At work it looks like throwing yourself at a new project so nobody, you included, has to mention the one that fell over. With a partner it's snapping about the bins when the real subject is the phone call on Tuesday. In the body it's the run pushed too hard and the jaw you've been clenching for days. Pushing won't get you through this one any quicker. Give the loss one proper hour, sitting down, phone in the other room, and say out loud what it was worth to you.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card lets an Aries Sun do what it was always going to do, which is skip the grief entirely. You're three steps into the next plan before anyone's finished saying sorry. It looks like resilience and people praise you for it. Underneath, a Mars that's been refused its feeling doesn't go away. It hardens into a short temper, a sudden competitiveness with someone who did nothing to you, a pride that won't admit anything was lost at all.

You'll see it at work as picking a fight with a colleague over something small, and in love as being suddenly, oddly unavailable. Friends ask how you are and get a brisk answer about your plans. Sometimes it flips and the anger turns inward, and you go flat and stop starting things, which for an Aries is the real warning light. Name the thing you lost to one person, in one sentence, and let them respond before you change the subject.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon calms down by doing something. A walk that turns into a run, a room rearranged at eleven at night, a row that clears the air and is forgotten by breakfast. The Five of Cups asks you to sit with a feeling that doing won't shift. There's a family tie between the two, since Mars rules your Moon's sign and Mars rules this card from Scorpio. The trouble is the elements. Your Moon is fire and the card is water, and those two either make steam or one puts the other out.

From the inside it feels like being cornered by your own emotions. You're used to feelings that flare and burn off within the hour. This one is Scorpio's kind, slow and heavy, and it's still there on the third morning, which frightens an Aries Moon more than it'll admit. You might find yourself crying and then furious about crying, or waking at four with your heart going and nothing to aim it at. That's the quincunx between the signs, a mismatch you keep having to adjust for in small ways all day.

Sleep is usually the first thing to go, and appetite swings between nothing and whatever's in the cupboard. With family it can come out as impatience with whoever's grieving at a different speed from you. At work you'll volunteer for everything so there's no quiet gap for it to get into. Let the body move the feeling without trying to outrun it. Walk somewhere with no destination and be sad while you do it, at walking pace.
moon.reversed:
When this card comes up reversed for an Aries Moon, the feeling has usually gone underground and set. You tell yourself it's handled. Then a small thing, a late train, a friend ten minutes behind, sets off a temper that's out of all proportion, and you're as surprised as they are. The Scorpio side of this Mars keeps score quietly while the Aries side insists it's moved on.

In the body it shows as tension that won't let go, restless legs in bed, headaches after long days. With the people closest to you it's picking fights you don't actually want to win. Most of that anger is grief that couldn't find a door. Write down, in one line, the loss you haven't let yourself be sad about. Then do something physical and slow with it in mind, digging a bed in the garden or swimming lengths.

rising.upright:
Aries rising usually comes into a room first and fast, hand already out. With the Five of Cups on that doorway, people meet someone who's clearly been knocked back and is working hard to hide it. Mars rules Aries, which makes it your chart ruler, and this card is Mars too, sitting in its other home sign. So the planet that shapes how you begin things has its head down over what it lost.

That's a very odd feeling for an Aries Ascendant. Your instinct is to act first and think later, and your instinct has just gone wrong, or at least the thing you went for didn't pay off. So you hesitate at the start of things, which you're not used to, and strangers read the hesitation as coolness or sadness depending on who's looking. It's fire and water again. The face wants to be bright and quick and the eyes give away something heavier, and people notice the gap before you do.

In a new job or a first meeting you may come across as guarded and serious. On a date it's the easy charm arriving slightly late, after a moment where you visibly decide whether to bother. With strangers generally you'll find you're picking fewer fights and listening a bit more, which isn't all bad. Let one person who's just met you see that you're having a hard stretch. A plain 'it's been a rough month' is plenty, and watch how much easier the conversation gets.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on an Aries Ascendant, this card tends to go one of two ways. Either you come in swinging, louder and brighter than usual so nobody could guess anything's wrong, or the first-in instinct stalls completely and you hang back at the edge of things for weeks. Both come from the same place, a loss you've decided not to be seen carrying.

At work the loud version starts new things and doesn't finish them, and the stalled version lets someone else take the lead you'd normally grab. Socially people find you either exhausting or oddly absent, and a new person tends to get a performance. Next time you walk into somewhere unfamiliar, go in at half speed. Say less in the first ten minutes and see what people offer you when you aren't rushing them.

sun.upright:
Taurus is the sign opposite Scorpio, which puts the Five of Cups right across the axis from your Sun. That axis is about keeping. Taurus keeps what's its own, the house, the savings, the routine, the person. Scorpio deals with what's shared and what gets lost. So the card holds up the thing you're best at, and shows you something you couldn't keep.

Mars is in detriment in Taurus, the sign opposite its own, so the card's planet has to work against the grain in your chart. Your Sun is steady and slow to anger and you'll take a lot before you move. When a loss lands, you don't rage. You dig in. I've known Taurus Suns carry a disappointment for years without mentioning it, still loyal to the plan that fell through, still paying into the thing that stopped paying back. The effort Mars has to make here comes out as stubbornness about the loss itself, a refusal to let it be over.

It shows most in money and in the body. A financial knock, even a small one, can dent your sense of who you are harder than it would for most people. In the body it's comfort eating, or sleeping longer and waking just as tired. With a partner it's being very calm on the surface and quietly withdrawn for weeks. Earth and water get on well, so things do grow back, slowly. Pick one solid thing that survived, a skill or a friendship or some savings, and spend an afternoon looking after it properly.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Taurus Sun can turn the loss into a fixture. You stop mentioning it and start arranging your life around it. Never that kind of job again, never lending money again, never letting that friend back in. Mars in detriment here is slow to act and very slow to stop, so it's the holding on that gets overdone, and it can harden into a quiet grudge that lasts for years.

In practice it's the bank balance you keep topping up out of fear, or the old possessions you can't part with because they belong to a version of things that ended. With family it's the silence round a subject everyone knows about. Choose one object tied to the loss and make a decision about it, keep it or give it away, and carry that decision out within the week.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon feels safe when things stay where you put them. The same mug, the same side of the bed, the same voice when you ring home. The Five of Cups is about something that didn't stay put, and for this Moon that registers first in the body, as a kind of disorientation, like reaching for a light switch that's been moved.

The card comes from Scorpio, directly opposite your Moon, so what it stirs up is the other half of your own need. You hold on, and Scorpio is the sign that has to let go. Your Moon's sign is also one of the two places where Mars sits in detriment, working uphill, so anger and grief move through you slowly and with effort, and you might not recognise either one by name. You just feel heavy and want the curtains drawn and can't see why the usual comforts aren't working. Often it's because the thing that's gone was one of them.

Eating and sleeping will tell you first. Either you want everything soft and familiar or you've gone off food you normally love. At home you might tidy the same drawer three times. With a partner you may want closeness without talking, which is fine as long as you tell them that's what it is. Earth and water are friendly elements, and your body really can help here. Cook something that takes hours, eat it slowly with someone you trust, and let the conversation go where it goes.
moon.reversed:
A Taurus Moon with this card upside down can make itself very comfortable around a loss it hasn't felt. Extra cushions, extra food, the same three programmes watched again. It all soothes and none of it touches the grief, which sits under the comfort like a stone under a blanket. Mars working against the grain here doesn't push. It waits, and the waiting can go on for years.

The body tends to carry it as sluggishness and a heaviness in the stomach, or as a resentment of change that seems to come from nowhere. At home you might resist any rearranging, even small changes, and get strangely upset when someone moves your stuff. Give up one comfort for a fortnight, the nightly glass of wine, the scrolling, the takeaway, and see what feeling turns up in the space it leaves.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising meets the world calmly. People read you as solid and unhurried, someone who won't be rattled, and usually they're right. With Taurus on the Ascendant, Scorpio falls on the cusp of your seventh house, the house of the people you pair up with, so the Five of Cups comes at you from the direction of other people. The loss on this card very often has a face.

Taurus is where Mars is in detriment, and the two signs are opposites, so the card pushes directly against your natural style. You'd like to keep the steady front going, and mostly you manage. There's a flatness people pick up on, though. You're slower to smile at strangers, slower to say yes to an invitation, slower to start anything. Some will read it as coldness. It's really the earth of your Ascendant soaking up the water of this card, and earth that's taken on that much water goes heavy and stays put.

In a job interview or a first meeting this comes across as seriousness, which plenty of people trust anyway. In a new relationship it's a reluctance to let anyone close while you're still sore from the last one, and a new person may feel they're being measured against someone who isn't in the room. Say one true thing early. You don't have to explain the loss, only admit there's been one, and people tend to relax around your steadiness again.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed on a Taurus Ascendant, the calm front can turn into a wall. Someone asks a friendly question and gets a pleasant, closed answer. You keep the pace slow and the doors shut, so smoothly that most people don't notice they've been kept out. The loss has made you wary of first steps of any kind.

In a job it looks like staying in the familiar role long after you've outgrown it, because starting again anywhere feels like exposing yourself. With new people it's politeness that never warms up. The body carries it as stiffness in the neck and shoulders, the posture of someone braced for impact. Next time you meet someone new, let them see one thing you care about, a book or a garden or a team you follow, and talk about it for longer than feels safe.

sun.upright:
Look at the figure on the Five of Cups, standing in a black cloak with its head down, and then think of a Gemini Sun, who'd normally be halfway through three stories at once. Gemini wants to find things out and pass them on and stay interested. Grief slows all of that down, and a loss that can't be talked out of is a strange thing for this Sun to come up against.

Mars has no special standing in Gemini. It's a visitor there and picks up the manner of Mercury, Gemini's ruler, so the card's force goes into the mind. You think about the loss from every angle and talk about it to everyone, and it feels like processing when it's mostly circling. Air and water don't fight, and they don't naturally meet either, so thoughts and feelings can run side by side for weeks without touching. Mars also rules the middle ten degrees of Gemini, whose card is the Nine of Swords, the one sitting up in bed with its head in its hands. That's this planet in your own sign, and it's why the thinking carries on into the small hours.

It shows up in your messages, the long texts at midnight explaining exactly why something went wrong. With a sibling or a close friend it's retelling the story until they run out of ways to help. At work you may be sharp and productive and oddly hollow by the end of the day. Try saying the loss to someone in a single sentence, with no explanation attached, and then stop talking and let them answer.
sun.reversed:
A Gemini Sun with this card reversed has often explained the loss away already. You've got a theory about why it happened, a joke about it, one version for work and another for friends, and none of them involve being sad. It keeps you busy and clever and moving, and it's quite tiring to watch from outside. The people close to you notice before you do.

It tends to show up as a sudden rush of new interests, a course signed up for, a trip booked, three projects started in a week. Or the Nine of Swords side takes over and it comes out as night-time anxiety about things that aren't really the problem. Say one thing about the loss that isn't clever. Just what it was and that you miss it, to one person who won't try to cheer you up.

moon.upright:
Words are how a Gemini Moon settles itself. You feel better once you've named something, told someone, read about it, worked out why. The Five of Cups doesn't go along with that. It's Mars in Scorpio, a heavy and private kind of feeling from a sign five away from yours, a quincunx, and your Moon keeps having to adjust to something it has no vocabulary for.

From the inside it's frustrating. You've talked it through twice and it hasn't shifted. You've read the articles. You still wake up with it. Mars is only a visitor in Gemini, taking its cues from Mercury, so the energy of the grief goes into your nerves, racing thoughts, trouble settling, six tabs open and none of them helping. Air and water are neutral to each other and have to be introduced. Your thinking and your feeling are both working very hard, in separate rooms.

Sleep is where it shows most. The mind replays the conversation, the decision, the text you sent. With a brother or sister, or a friend who's as good as one, you might keep bringing the subject round, needing them to agree it wasn't your fault. At work your concentration comes and goes in bursts. Before bed, write the whole thing out on paper, by hand and as messily as you like, then close the notebook and leave it in another room.
moon.reversed:
When the Five of Cups turns over for a Gemini Moon, the feeling can get talked about so much that it stops being felt. Every friend has heard the story. You're funny about it. It has a beginning, a middle and an end, and the actual sadness has gone somewhere you can't reach. Mars rules part of your sign through the Nine of Swords, and that's usually where the unspoken bit turns up, as worry at three in the morning.

It can show as jumpiness in the body, a nervous stomach, a phone you can't put down. With friends there's lots of contact and none of it goes very deep. Pick one person and tell them you don't want advice. Then say the part of the story you've been leaving out, and let it sit there without a joke after it.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising usually gets into a conversation within a minute of arriving, curious and light, with a question ready. Drawn for that doorway, the Five of Cups makes the lightness harder to find. People still meet someone clever and easy to talk to, and then there's a pause where your attention drifts off somewhere they can't follow.

Mars has no rank in Gemini. It's a guest, borrowing Mercury's manner, so the card's weight gets expressed through talk. You may catch yourself telling near-strangers more than you meant to, a line about the break-up or the redundancy dropped into small talk at the bus stop. Or you go the other way and chat brightly about nothing so nobody gets near it. Air and water aren't natural friends, and your easy social manner and this heavy feeling don't sit comfortably on one face. Instinct suffers a bit too. The quick read you usually have on people comes slower, and you second-guess it.

In a new job this looks like being liked straight away and finding the small talk oddly tiring by mid-afternoon. On a first date it's being good company and then telling them, over the second drink, something you'd meant to save for the fifth. Neither of these is a disaster. When you meet someone new, decide which true thing you'd be willing to say and say it early, on purpose, so it doesn't leak out sideways later.
rising.reversed:
Turned upside down, this card can leave a Gemini Ascendant chattering over a gap. You're brilliant company. You've a funny story for every situation and a question ready for every silence, and nobody who's just met you would guess there's been a loss. The ones who've known you longer notice you haven't said anything real in weeks, and some of them have stopped asking.

At work the quickness turns scattered, emails answered in half-sentences, meetings where you're charming and only half there. Socially it's the party you leave early without saying goodbye. Next time you start a conversation with someone new, slow it down. Ask one thing and wait for the whole answer, even if it takes a while and goes somewhere sad.

sun.upright:
A Cancer Sun is built to look after things, the people, the house, the old photos, the family story. So when the Five of Cups turns up, the loss is nearly always something you were keeping safe. Both signs are water and they sit four apart in a trine, which means this card's feeling moves into you with no resistance at all. You understand grief like this without anyone explaining it, and it can fill you up fast.

Mars is in fall in Cancer. The planet of direct action is at its weakest in your sign and has to go the long way round, and for you that means the anger inside grief rarely comes out straight. You won't shout at the person who let you down. You'll be hurt and go quiet and cook for everyone anyway, and then feel resentful that nobody noticed. The water doubles up as well. Same element, same language, and a feeling that deep can carry you off with it for a while.

Home is where it shows most, in the family, in who's being looked after and who isn't. With a parent an old loss may surface just when you'd thought it was dealt with. At work you can find yourself mothering a whole team through a disappointment while nobody checks on you. Let someone look after you for one evening. Tell them what happened and ask them to make the tea.
sun.reversed:
Reversed on a Cancer Sun, the card tends to turn the loss into a shell. You pull right in, look after everyone else with great care, and let absolutely nobody look after you. With Mars in fall here, the hurt can't go out, so it goes round and round the inside and becomes a kind of wounded loyalty to what's gone.

In the family it shows as going over old grievances, and in the house as keeping things exactly as they were. You can be sentimental in a way that's really a refusal. People you love may feel held at arm's length by someone who's being very kind to them. Make one small change at home that you've been avoiding. Move the chair or clear the shelf, and let yourself feel whatever it brings up without making it anyone else's job to fix.

moon.upright:
Tears come easily for a Cancer Moon, and so does memory. A smell or an old song and you're back somewhere. The Five of Cups lands on that like rain on wet ground. It's water on water, the same element, and the trine between Scorpio and Cancer means nothing slows the feeling down on its way in.

The Moon rules Cancer, so your Moon is in its own sign and you feel fully and know it. The complication is that Mars falls in Cancer. The part of grief that's anger, the part that says this wasn't fair and wants something done, gets no voice here. It turns into worry and clinginess, a need to check everyone's all right, three calls to your mother in a day. You may find you can cry about it easily and can't get cross about it at all, and that the crying doesn't quite finish the job.

The body carries it in the stomach and in sleep. You might not want to eat, or want only the food you had as a child. With family, old losses tend to wake up alongside the new one, and you'll find yourself thinking about a grandparent or a house you left years ago. With a partner you'll need a lot of holding and may not ask for it. Ask anyway. Say you need a quiet night in and a hand on your back, and let them do it.
moon.reversed:
Upside down for a Cancer Moon, this card can leave you stuck in the tide of it. The sorrow becomes the mood of the house. Everything reminds you of what's gone and you keep the reminders close, the voicemail you won't delete, the jumper still on the chair. With the water doubled and Mars too weak here to push you out, the feeling can settle into a very comfortable sadness.

Or the shell closes and you look after everyone as a way of feeling none of it yourself. Family meals, favours, all the birthday cards on time. Sleep goes strange either way. Spend an hour with the thing you're keeping, the photo or the message, and cry properly if it comes. Then put it somewhere safe that isn't in your eyeline every day.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising tends to approach new people sideways, warm but careful, testing the ground first. With this card on your Ascendant, the careful part is winning. People meet you and sense softness and something protected, a friendliness that doesn't quite open the door. Both signs are water and a trine apart, so the grief sits naturally on your face. You don't have to perform it, and you'd struggle to hide it.

The Mars side is harder. Mars is the push that gets things started, and in Cancer it's in fall and at its weakest, so starting anything new is heavy going. Instinct says wait, stay near what's familiar, don't risk another spill. You may notice you're taking the long way round everything. Going to the party and staying in the kitchen with the one person you know. Applying for the job and then never following up.

Strangers will probably read you as kind and a bit sad, and some will open up to you because of it, which is lovely and also draining. At work you'll likely seem quieter in meetings than your reputation would suggest. In a new relationship you'll want reassurance early. Choose one new thing to begin and make the first step very small, a single email or a coffee, so the weak Mars doesn't have to carry much.
rising.reversed:
With this card reversed, Cancer rising can go fully into the shell. You're pleasant and helpful and completely unreachable. People who've just met you may take you for shy, or aloof, and people who know you see the difference straight away. Home starts to feel like the only safe place, and the instinct to protect yourself takes over the whole doorway.

It shows up as turning down invitations with lovely excuses, and at work as doing everything you're asked and volunteering nothing. Mars in fall means the anger in the loss comes out sideways, as sulking or a pointed silence toward someone who isn't sure what they did. Say yes to one invitation you'd normally dodge. Stay for an hour, and let one person ask how you've been.

sun.upright:
Leo and Scorpio are both fixed signs, three apart, which makes them square, and a square is friction that won't let up until somebody does something about it. That's the Five of Cups meeting a Leo Sun. Leo wants to be warm and generous and seen, and proud of what it's made. For Leo a loss is rarely just sad. It's a blow to the pride as well, and that part is much harder to talk about.

Mars is only a visitor in Leo, lit by the Sun, so whatever it does gets done in public. You feel the grief and also feel watched while you're feeling it. Fire and water are opposed elements, and that's the struggle in a sentence. The fire in you wants to keep the smile up and host the dinner anyway, and the card's water keeps putting it out. Mars does own the last ten degrees of Leo, where the card is the Seven of Wands, one person on a ridge holding off six. That's the Leo answer to a loss. You defend it, insist it was the right call, and you're a bit stubborn about it, which you probably know.

It tends to show up in creative work, the project or the performance that didn't land the way you'd pictured. With a child, or someone you've mentored, it can be the disappointment of watching them choose a different road from the one you hoped for. In love it's feeling unappreciated and too proud to say so. Tell one person the part you're embarrassed about, the bit where you'd hoped for more, and let them see it without making a joke of it first.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Sun, the Five of Cups can turn grief into a performance of being fine. The bigger laugh, the brighter clothes, the party thrown the weekend after it all fell apart. The square between these two fixed signs means neither side gives, so the loss stays exactly where it was under all that warmth, and the warmth starts to feel like work.

Or it goes the other way into wounded pride, and you pull out of anything where you might be seen to fail again. People around you notice the sulk more than the sadness. At work it's refusing to pitch again after one rejection. In love it's waiting for the other person to make the first move, and minding when they don't. Go back to the thing that stung, once, in some small way nobody's watching.

moon.upright:
The figure in the Five of Cups has turned away from everything, cloak up, head down, and that's about the last posture a Leo Moon would choose. You feel best when you're loved out loud, told, chosen, and you give it back in armfuls. This card usually means that warmth has gone from somewhere, a friend gone quiet, a love cooled, an ending you didn't pick.

Leo is fixed fire and Scorpio is fixed water, and the square between them is the kind of friction that won't settle until you act on it. Feelings in a Leo Moon are big and loyal and they last. So does this card's grief. The two together make a hurt that won't budge and a pride that won't let you admit how much it hurts. Mars has no dignity in Leo and borrows the Sun's light, so even your sadness wants an audience of one. You'd like the right person to notice you're upset without being told.

At home it can come out as drama about small things, the burnt toast, the late bus, because the big thing is too tender to touch. With a partner it's waiting to be asked. With friends it's going very quiet in the group chat, which for you is a loud signal and one they may miss. The body often feels it as heat and restlessness and trouble dropping off to sleep. Ask for the warmth you're missing, directly, from someone who has it to give.
moon.reversed:
When the card flips for a Leo Moon, pride usually takes over from grief. You decide you're offended instead of hurt, and offence is much easier to live with. The fixed square keeps it going. A slight from months back gets rehearsed in the shower. The person who left gets written out of the story, or written in as the villain, and neither version lets you miss them.

It shows up in friendships as loyalty tests people don't know they're sitting. With family it's a coldness that surprises everyone, including you. Sleep runs hot and late. Think of one person you've been quietly punishing for a loss that wasn't entirely their doing, and send them something warm and ordinary, a photo or a joke, with no mention of any of it.

rising.upright:
Leo rising usually gets noticed walking in and doesn't mind a bit. With this card on the Ascendant, people still notice, and what they see is someone who's plainly been through something and is holding their head up about it. The Sun rules Leo, so it's your chart ruler, and a front run by the Sun finds it hard to look anything but bright. The Five of Cups makes that a lot of effort.

Leo and Scorpio are square, both fixed, and fire and water pull in opposite directions. On the doorway of the chart that shows as a face working against itself. You want to be generous and open with strangers, and the hurt keeps closing you up mid-sentence. Mars is a guest in Leo with no standing of its own, and it borrows the Sun's need to be seen, so even the grief comes out a little public. The Seven of Wands, Mars's card in the last ten degrees of Leo, shows the instinct underneath, which is to hold the high ground and not let anyone see you wobble.

At work you might seem prouder and pricklier than usual, especially if the loss was a professional one. In a new friendship you'll be great company for an hour and then go cool without warning. On a first date you may oversell yourself a bit. Let one new person see the dented version. Say something honest about a rough patch and notice that they don't think any less of you.
rising.reversed:
The act gets turned up a notch when this card lands reversed on a Leo Ascendant. More sparkle, louder stories, a bigger entrance to cover what's missing. Some people buy it completely. The ones who look twice see how tired the face is by the end of the evening, and how quickly it drops when you think nobody's watching. Leo is fixed, so this can go on a long time.

Or the pride goes into hiding instead. You stop turning up to things where you'd normally shine, and people assume you've gone off them. At work it's the presentation you pass to someone else. Socially it's saying you're busy. Go to one thing you'd normally light up, stay quiet there if you need to, and leave when you're ready.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns like to be useful, and they like things to work. When something goes wrong you're the one making the list of what happens next. This card brings a loss no list will fix, and that's hard on a Sun whose pride is in being competent. You've probably already worked out exactly where it went wrong, and found it wasn't much comfort.

Scorpio and Virgo are two signs apart, a sextile, and earth and water are friendly, so this pairing can actually work for you. A sextile is an opening, though, and it has to be used. Mars has no rank in Virgo and takes on Mercury's manner there, analytical, critical, very good at detail. Aimed at a loss, that turns into an audit. Every decision gets gone over, and the one who comes off worst is usually you. I see plenty of Virgo Suns who'll forgive anyone except themselves, and this card brings that out.

A mistake at work, yours or someone else's, gets turned over long after it's useful. In the body it's the tight stomach and the list-making at bedtime. With a friend who's hurting too, you'll be brilliant at practical help and find it harder to just sit with them. Let the earth side help. Do one useful thing for the loss, sort the paperwork or return the borrowed things, and then stop. Leave the rest of the audit undone.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun can end up grading its own grief when this card is reversed. Am I sad enough, too sad, sad for too long. Or you skip it and get very, very efficient, the house spotless, every form filled in, and no room anywhere for what happened. Mars in Mercury's sign gets fussy when it's blocked, and small things start to feel unbearable.

Projects stall on perfectionism, and at home you snap about crumbs. The body often keeps the score as tension, a jaw or a stomach that won't unclench. Write down one thing you did right in the situation that went wrong. It'll be harder to find than the mistakes. Keep going until you've got it.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon feels safe when there's something useful to do with its hands. Tidy the kitchen, fix the bike, sort out somebody else's problem, and the mood lifts. The Five of Cups doesn't give you much to fix. The cups have already spilled, and grief has no tasks, which is exactly what makes it so hard for this Moon to bear.

The good news is that earth and water help each other, and Scorpio is only two signs from Virgo, a sextile, so the feeling can move through you if you give it a route. Mars is a guest in Virgo, shaped by Mercury, and in feeling terms that makes the grief busy and nervous. You worry about the small things around it, whether you said the right thing at the funeral, whether you should have noticed sooner. The body keeps a close watch on itself too. You might notice every twinge and read it as a sign something's wrong.

Routines are where this shows. You'll either cling to them or they'll fall apart entirely, and both are telling you something. At work it can look like doing other people's jobs so you've no time to think. With a partner it's fussing over them when you're the one who needs looking after. Keep one small daily ritual going for the grief itself, ten minutes with a cup of tea on the back step, and let that be the task.
moon.reversed:
When this card sits reversed on a Virgo Moon, the feeling tends to get converted into worry. It's easier to be anxious about your health, your inbox, the state of the fridge, than to be sad about what you actually lost. Mars with no standing in Mercury's sign turns fretful, and the fretting has endless material. Every small problem gets your full attention because the big one gets none.

You'll notice it in sleep, which goes light and broken, and in a sharpness with the people you live with. Friends might hear lots about your symptoms and nothing about your heart. At work you'll find errors in everything. Sit down with the actual loss for a quarter of an hour, with no task attached, and let whatever turns up be untidy. Then go and make dinner.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as capable and a bit reserved, the person who's spotted your shoelace is undone before you have. With the Five of Cups here, that careful manner pulls tighter. People meet someone composed and helpful who clearly isn't sleeping well, and they aren't sure which one to respond to.

Mercury rules Virgo, so it's your chart ruler, and Mars has no special dignity in your rising sign and takes its colour from Mercury there. The card's force runs through your ruling planet's filter. You meet the world by analysing it, and after a loss you tend to analyse it for danger. First meetings get run through twice on the way home. Scorpio and Virgo are sextile, and the elements get on, so the grief doesn't wreck your front. It gives it a certain seriousness, and makes you slow to start anything new in case that goes wrong too.

At work people might find you sharper than usual, especially with new ideas. On a first date you'll be polite and observant and give away very little. In a new group you'll make yourself useful straight away, which helps them like you and keeps them from knowing you. Pick one situation where you'd normally help, and let someone help you instead. Hand them the task and don't check it.
rising.reversed:
With this card upside down, a Virgo Ascendant can hide behind being useful. You arrive with the spreadsheet, the plan, the offer to help set up, and nobody gets to ask how you are because you're always busy. It works well and people are grateful for it. They just don't get to know you, and after a while they stop expecting to.

Or the self-criticism goes on show, and you apologise for things nobody noticed. At work it looks like over-preparing for every meeting. Socially it's leaving early to finish something. In the body it can feel like a stomach in knots before anything new. Next time you're introduced to someone, don't offer to help with anything. Ask them a question and stay put.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns build themselves around fairness and around other people. You're at your best in a pair, or keeping a room in balance, or making something lovely. This is a lopsided card, all the attention on three spilled cups and none on the two behind, and a loss that feels unfair gets under a Libra Sun's skin like almost nothing else.

Libra is one of the two signs where Mars is in detriment. The planet of wanting and fighting works against the grain here, because your instinct is to smooth things over and see the other side. So your anger about this loss is hard to reach. You can see why the other person did what they did. You can argue their case better than they could. Underneath all that fairness is a hurt that hasn't been allowed to say anything unfair. Scorpio sits right next door, a semi-sextile, and neighbouring signs have what the other lacks. Scorpio doesn't mind taking sides.

In a relationship it shows as being reasonable for weeks and then finding yourself crying over the washing-up. With a business partner or a close friend it can be the agreement that fell through and the calm email you rewrote six times. At work it's being gracious about someone else getting the thing you wanted. Let yourself be unfair about it, privately, for ten minutes. Say out loud everything you'd never say to their face, and then leave it there.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with this card reversed can get very good at keeping the peace over a loss nobody's allowed to mention. Everyone's getting on. It's all terribly civilised. The resentment leaks into your tone, the slight edge on 'that's fine', and with Mars so weak in your sign it rarely gets any further than that. People sense it and can't name it.

In love it's agreeing to everything and feeling further away each week. With friends it's playing go-between in someone else's falling-out while ignoring your own. At work it's the polite reply to an unfair decision. Choose one small thing you've gone along with and say, plainly and without softening it, that you mind. Then leave the silence alone.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon needs things to be all right between people. A cross word left hanging can spoil a whole evening, and a nice room with the right company can mend nearly anything. The Five of Cups brings a sadness that company doesn't lift, which is disorienting. You go out, you see friends, it's lovely, and you come home and it's still sitting there.

Scorpio is Libra's neighbour, the next sign along, and the two have very little in common. You process feelings by talking them through and weighing them up. Scorpio feels them to the bottom, in private. Air and water are neutral and have to be introduced to each other. Mars is in detriment in Libra, so the part of grief that's angry or wants to hit back gets pushed well out of sight, because anger feels ugly to this Moon. It tends to come out as tiredness, or as being exceptionally nice to everyone.

In a partnership it's needing reassurance and feeling silly about needing it. With friends it's saying yes to every plan so you're never alone with the feeling. You may sleep fine and find waking up hard. Find one person who can sit with you in the sad part without trying to make it nicer, and tell them that's the job.
moon.reversed:
For a Libra Moon, the reversed card tends to put a pleasant face on grief. The house is lovely, the conversation is light, and the loss has been tidied into a corner where it won't upset anyone. That takes a great deal of upkeep. Mars can't get much done in Libra, and the anger inside the sadness just sits under the niceness, going a bit sour.

It shows up as indecision about things that shouldn't matter, which café, which colour, because the real decision, whether to feel this at all, is being put off. With a partner it can be a sudden coolness you both pretend isn't there. Tell someone you trust the unfair version of what happened, the one where you're simply hurt, and don't balance it with their side.

rising.upright:
Libra rising charms people. You meet the world with a smile and a way of making everyone feel they've been listened to. The Five of Cups leaves the smile in place and puts something wistful under it, and people pick up on that within a few minutes. Aries sits on your seventh house, and Mars rules Aries, so this card's planet is the one that describes your partners. The loss often came through one of them.

In Libra itself Mars is in detriment, working uphill, and that's the approach problem. Your instinct is to make things pleasant and this card wants you to admit they aren't. You end up very gracious in public and flattened in private. Libra and Scorpio are neighbouring signs, and Scorpio has the one thing Libra finds hardest, a willingness to let a room go quiet and heavy. Strangers can feel you choosing not to go there.

In a job interview you'll be warm and a touch too agreeable, and might undersell yourself to keep the mood nice. On a date you'll be lovely company and not entirely present. With new colleagues you'll smooth over every awkward moment, including the ones that could have been useful. Let one awkward pause run. Next time a conversation goes quiet, leave it quiet for five seconds and see what the other person says.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, the card can make a Libra Ascendant's charm work overtime. Every first meeting gets the full treatment, the compliments, the laugh, the effort to make sure everyone's comfortable, and you come away exhausted. It's harder than usual to start anything alone. Mars rules your seventh house, and you find yourself waiting for other people to make the first move.

It can show at work as agreeing to terms you don't like because arguing felt rude. In love it's staying in a pleasant arrangement that stopped meaning much a while ago. Pick one first conversation and go into it without trying to be liked. Be friendly, be honest, and let them make up their own minds.

sun.upright:
This is one of Scorpio's own cards. Every sign is split into three ten-degree slices, and the Five of Cups belongs to the first slice of Scorpio, ruled by Mars, which is also the sign's traditional ruler. So with a Scorpio Sun there's no translating to do. The card speaks your language with the authority of the planet that owns the place.

Mars at home in Scorpio is Mars at full strength, pointed inward, and grief like that goes all the way down. You don't do half-feelings. When you lose something you'll stand over it until you understand exactly what happened and why. Scorpio's Major is Death, the card of endings that clear the ground, and you know better than most that some things have to be let go of properly. The difficulty is the doubled water. Same element, nothing to slow it, and moving on can start to feel like a betrayal of what you lost.

At work it can show as loyalty to a failed project or a departed boss that everyone else dropped long ago. In love it's refusing to be comforted until you've got to the bottom of it, which can shut a partner out. With family it's the old wound you still know the exact shape of. Pick a day and a place to mark the loss properly, on your own terms, and when it's done, walk home by a different route.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun with this card reversed can let grief harden into something colder. A grudge that's kept polished. A private decision never to need anyone that much again. Mars at home here has all the stamina in the world, and turned the wrong way it spends that stamina keeping score. You may not even feel sad, only very clear about who's on the list.

At work it's working twice as hard to prove a point to someone who left long ago. With a former partner it's still checking their profile. With friends it's a loyalty test they don't know they failed. In the body it's a jaw set hard by evening. Choose one name on that list and take it off. You don't have to tell them. Stop keeping the file.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel things at full depth and tell almost nobody. You need privacy, loyalty and the truth, in roughly that order, and you'd sooner be alone than with people who don't get it. This card is your Moon's home ground. It's Mars in the first ten degrees of Scorpio, the sign's own ruler, so the grief on this card is exactly the kind you're built to feel.

Water on water, the same element, and no brake anywhere. That's why it can be so consuming. You may find yourself replaying one conversation at three in the morning with total recall, every word, every pause. Mars is strong and unforced in Scorpio, which puts real force behind the feeling, and that force wants somewhere to go. Often it goes into investigation. You want to know what really happened, who knew, when it turned. Your Moon will follow a feeling a long way down before it comes back up, and it won't be hurried.

Sleep suffers most. With a partner, you may want them close and not want to explain, which is a lot to ask of anyone who can't read minds. With friends you'll pull back and let one person in, if that. The body often holds it as tightness low in the belly or a heavy tiredness in the limbs. Choose the one person who gets to know, tell them properly, and let them see you when you aren't composed.
moon.reversed:
Shut is the word for a Scorpio Moon with this card reversed. The grief goes into the vault and the door's locked, and you're so good at seeming fine that people who've known you for years wouldn't guess. It isn't gone. Mars in its own sign doesn't lose energy, it goes quiet and waits, and sometimes it surfaces years later over something small.

In practice it shows as suspicion in relationships, jealousy that has little to do with the person in front of you, or a flat refusal to discuss a certain subject. The body might carry it as tiredness that sleep doesn't touch. Write the thing you've never said about this loss on a piece of paper, all of it. Burn it afterwards if you like, once it's down in full.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already gives people the feeling you know more than you're saying. You watch before you speak, and very few get past the first layer. Put the Five of Cups on that and the watchfulness has a wound behind it. People can sense it even when they couldn't tell you what it is.

Mars rules Scorpio, which makes it your chart ruler, and this card is Mars at home in the opening ten degrees of your rising sign. It's the landlord's own card, so it speaks in the sign's own voice. Same element too, water on water, so your way of approaching the world and the grief on this card sit together with no friction at all, which isn't always a good thing. Your instinct is already to hold back, test people and keep your own counsel. After a loss those instincts get stronger, and a new person gets tested before they've done anything.

At work people may find you intimidating, particularly anyone new. On a date you'll ask sharp questions and answer very few. In a new place you'll take a long while deciding who to trust, and that's partly sensible and partly grief doing the deciding. Try letting one new person see something small and unguarded, a laugh at your own expense or a line about the loss that doesn't need handling.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on Scorpio rising, the watchful front can turn into armour. You meet new people with a look that says they'll have to earn it, and most don't bother trying. Your chart ruler is sitting in its own sign on this card, so there's real power in the guard, and it keeps people at a distance with very little effort from you.

It shows up at work as a reputation for being hard to read, which can cost you an opportunity or two. With someone new in your life it's testing them until they give up. There can be a pull toward secrecy about the loss as well, as though telling would give someone power over you. Tell one person who's new to your life what happened, in two sentences, and watch what they do with it.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius is the sign that comes straight after Scorpio, and in a lot of ways it's the sign of climbing out from under it. You're built for the horizon. Meaning, travel, the next big idea, a joke at the worst moment that somehow helps. The Five of Cups asks you to stay down in the Scorpio part of the story longer than you'd like, standing over the spilled cups before you go looking for the bridge.

Neighbouring signs rarely have much in common, and each has what the other lacks. Scorpio has patience with pain. Sagittarius has faith that it'll all turn out. Mars has no standing in your sign and takes on Jupiter's colour there, generous and restless and keen to call everything a lesson. Add fire against water and you get the pull of this pairing. You want to find the meaning quickly and head off with it, and the card's water keeps dousing that. The lesson you've settled on feels a bit thin, even to you.

It shows up in plans. The trip booked the week after the break-up, the new course started the day after the rejection. With friends it's being the funny one about it, which they'll let you be, up to a point. With your beliefs it can be a real wobble, a sense that the thing you trusted to make sense of life hasn't covered this. Before you book anything, spend a weekend at home with the loss, and let it be pointless for two days.
sun.reversed:
A Sagittarius Sun can simply leave when this card turns over. A new city, a new plan, a new philosophy, and a cheerful refusal to look back. From outside it looks like optimism. Mars in Jupiter's sign has plenty of fuel for running, and the grief comes along in the luggage anyway. Or the faith cracks and you turn preachy and bitter, telling everyone how the world really works.

It shows up in relationships as bolting when things get heavy, and at work as quitting something before you've let yourself feel how much you wanted it. Friends get the adventures and never the sad bits. Before your next big move, sit down with one person who knew you before the loss and tell them honestly how it's been.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. Open plans, open roads, a sense that tomorrow could look different. You recover from most things by getting some distance, a long walk or a long drive or a plane ticket. The Five of Cups closes the road a bit. The feeling it brings wants you to stay put, and staying put is the one thing that makes this Moon properly anxious.

Scorpio is the sign just behind yours, and neighbours like that each have what the other lacks. Scorpio can sit in a dark room with a feeling. Your Moon would much sooner open a window. Fire and water are the opposed elements, so there's real friction, the restless, hopeful part of you clashing with a sadness that won't be cheered up. Mars in Sagittarius has no rank and borrows Jupiter's largeness, so when it hits, it hits big, and then you swing hard the other way, planning, joking, booking things. The mood can go up and down like that several times a day.

Sleep can go erratic, and you might feel restless in your own home. With family it's the urge to be anywhere but the room where it happened. With friends it's being great company at the pub and quiet on the walk home. The body wants movement, and that's fine, as long as the sad bits are allowed to come too. Take the long walk, on your own and without headphones, and don't plan anything while you're on it.
moon.reversed:
Turned over for a Sagittarius Moon, the card often means the feeling's been outrun. You're already on to the next thing, full of plans, and the grief gets a single line in a conversation, delivered with a shrug. Mars in a fire sign with no dignity to steady it can burn through a feeling so fast it never properly lands.

It shows in the body as restlessness, the itch to be elsewhere, poor sleep in your own bed. With the people you love it's a cheerfulness that leaves them feeling shut out. Sometimes it turns into a quiet cynicism instead, which sits badly on you. Go back to one place connected to the loss, or look at one photo, and stay with it past the point where it's comfortable.

rising.upright:
First impressions are easy for Sagittarius rising. Open face, big laugh, a way of treating strangers like people you've known for years. Drawn for your Ascendant, the Five of Cups leaves that openness in place, and there's a flicker of something else behind it that people catch when the laughing stops.

Jupiter rules Sagittarius, so it's your chart ruler, and Mars in your rising sign is a visitor with Jupiter's colouring, bold and quick to try things. The card's water gets in the way. Fire and water are opposed, and at the doorway of the chart that shows as starting things with the old enthusiasm and running out of it halfway. There's another layer too. Scorpio is the sign just before yours, which puts it on your twelfth house, the house of what's kept out of sight, and that's where this card's grief tends to sit for you.

People you've just met will find you as friendly as ever and slightly less reliable, promising the drink and then cancelling. At work you might start something new with a big speech and find you've no stomach for the detail. On a first date you'll be funny, and they may leave feeling they haven't met you. Let one new person hear the serious version of you. Tell them something that happened this year, plainly, with no punchline.
rising.reversed:
The bluntness sharpens when this card is reversed for Sagittarius rising. You say the tactless thing, laugh it off, and move on before anyone can react. Underneath there's a hurt looking for an exit, and the cheerful directness gives it one. Or you go the other way, your usual openness shuts down, and strangers meet someone oddly flat. Neither is much like you.

At work it shows as starting new things and abandoning them, or picking arguments about principles that are really about something else. Socially it's making plans for a group and then not turning up. Next time you feel the urge to leave early or say something cutting, stay ten more minutes and say something kind instead. Notice what that costs you.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns measure themselves by what they've built. The career, the savings, the reputation, the family that can depend on them. Mars is exalted in Capricorn, which is to say it's an honoured guest there, at its most disciplined and effective, and you'd think that would make the Five of Cups easy to handle. Mostly it makes it easy to work through, and that's a slightly different thing.

Scorpio and Capricorn are a sextile apart and the elements are friendly, so you've got resources here. You can take a loss and build a structure round it. Mars also rules the middle ten degrees of Capricorn, whose card is the Three of Pentacles, the stonemason at work in the church. That's often how you grieve, by going back to work and doing it very well. The tension is that an exalted Mars can run on discipline for months while the sadness sits unexamined. I've watched Capricorn Suns handle a loss like a bad quarter, efficiently, and then wonder why they're so tired.

It shows most in your career, especially if the loss is a job or a title or a plan you'd worked years toward. With a parent, or anyone you feel responsible for, it's being the strong one at the expense of being the sad one. In the body it can be the back and the knees, the places that carry weight. Book the time off you'd tell anyone else to take, and don't fill it with jobs round the house.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card can push a Capricorn Sun into overdrive. The loss gets managed. You take on more work, more responsibility, a harder target, and you tell yourself the busyness is resilience. Exalted Mars has an enormous capacity for effort, and when it's blocked that capacity becomes a way of never stopping long enough to feel anything. Or the ambition drains away and you stop trying at the thing that hurt you.

At work it looks like being impressive and joyless. At home it's missing things, the dinner, the birthday, and explaining why that was necessary. The people who love you feel they're getting the leftover hours. Pick one evening a week where you stop at six and do nothing useful, and keep it even when something urgent comes up.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when it's coping. You like being the one who's got it handled, lists made, feelings kept for later, preferably in private. The Five of Cups brings a feeling that won't be kept for later, and it has a habit of arriving just as you've finished being strong for everyone else.

Water and earth are friendly elements, and Scorpio and Capricorn sit a sextile apart, so there's an opening here, one that still needs using. Mars is exalted in Capricorn, a planet at its most capable, and in feeling terms that gives you a great deal of self-control. You can hold grief for a very long time without it showing. The cost is that the body ends up holding it for you. Stiff shoulders, tension headaches, a tiredness that's in the bones. You might even feel faintly ashamed of being sad at all, as if it were a kind of inefficiency.

At home it can show as being very practical about a loss, sorting the papers, organising the clear-out, and then sitting in the car for twenty minutes before going in. With a parent it may bring up an old sense of having had to grow up early. At work you'll keep functioning and people will say you're amazing. Give the feeling a structure, since structure is what your Moon trusts. Set aside half an hour on a Sunday, same time each week, for nothing except missing what's gone.
moon.reversed:
Turned the other way, the card can freeze a Capricorn Moon. The feeling gets filed. You're fine, busy, reliable, a bit cold, and people have stopped asking because the answer's always the same. Exalted Mars gives you the stamina to keep the lid on almost indefinitely, which is what makes it risky. A lid kept on that long tends to come off at a bad moment.

It shows up in the body as stiffness and poor sleep, and with loved ones as impatience with anyone who's openly upset. You may be quite hard on someone else's grief without meaning to be. Tell one person, briefly and without apology, that you're coping less well than it looks. Then let them do something for you.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising meets new people with a handshake and a straight face, and earns their trust slowly. You come across as older than your years, or at least more serious, and people tend to assume you're in charge. Add this card and the seriousness deepens. Strangers see someone composed and a bit weighed down.

Saturn rules Capricorn and so rules your chart, and Mars is exalted in your rising sign, the planet at its most disciplined and honoured. So even grieving, you look capable, and people might have no idea anything's happened. The sextile between Scorpio and Capricorn, and the easy mix of earth and water, let the loss sit quite naturally behind your composure. Your instinct is to hold steady, and it works. What slips is the warmth. You're slower to smile and more guarded about anything new, and a new colleague might decide you don't like them.

At work this can look like being handed more responsibility because you seem so steady, at exactly the moment you'd like less. In a new relationship it's taking a long time to let anyone see you're human. With strangers you'll be polite and closed. Let one professional contact know you've had a hard year. Say it in one sentence, in your normal voice, and carry on.
rising.reversed:
Composure hardens into a wall of competence for Capricorn rising with the card upside down. You're so on top of things that nobody would dare ask how you are. First impressions are of someone efficient, a bit severe, possibly unimpressed. Exalted Mars keeps the machine running whatever's happening underneath, and the people who might help take one look and decide you don't need them.

At work it can show as micromanaging, or taking on everything so nothing can go wrong again. In new relationships it's a formality that never loosens. Your knees and back may be carrying some of it. Next time you're introduced to someone, tell them one thing you're hopeless at. Keep it light, and see how the conversation changes.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns like to stand a little back from things and see the whole pattern. You're independent, principled, loyal to friends and to ideas, and not especially keen on big emotional scenes. The Five of Cups is a big emotional scene, only a quiet one. The figure in the black cloak isn't thinking about systems. They're standing over what they lost.

Aquarius and Scorpio are fixed signs three apart, a square, and squares force the issue. Both of you are stubborn. Scorpio holds on to a feeling and Aquarius holds on to a position, so when you lose something you may take a very firm view of it very quickly. It was for the best. It was always going to happen. Air and water don't know each other well, so you can know you're grieving without quite feeling it. Mars has no dignity in Aquarius and takes Saturn's colouring there, cool and patient and quite good at detachment.

It tends to show up with friends, where you're supportive to everyone else in the group and oddly absent about your own news. With a cause or a community you care about, the loss might be a falling-out or a disillusionment. At work you'll analyse what went wrong and write a sensible document about it. Tell one friend the unreasonable part, the bit where you're just sad, without the analysis round it.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun can go very cool indeed when this card turns over. You're rational about the loss, even interested in it, and anyone who expects tears gets a thoughtful explanation. The fixed square keeps that stance in place, and the feeling stays exactly where it was, underneath the reasoning. Or the stubbornness turns outward and you fall out with a whole group over a principle that's really about something else.

In love it can look like a sudden need for space. With friends it's cutting someone off over a disagreement that isn't the real issue. The body might carry it as a restless, jangly tiredness. Choose one person and tell them, in feeling words only and with no reasons, what you lost and how it's been.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon soothes itself with space. A bit of distance, a friend to talk ideas over with, the sense that you're free to come and go. Feelings are fine as long as you can step back and look at them. The Five of Cups doesn't give you that step back. Its grief is Scorpio's, from a fixed water sign square to your fixed air one, and it keeps pulling you in close.

From the inside it's an odd split. You can describe your sadness very clearly, almost like a case study, and still wake up with a weight on your chest. Air and water are neutral to each other and need introducing, and in you they may never have properly met. Mars carries no rank in Aquarius and takes on the colour of Saturn, the sign's traditional ruler, and Saturn keeps things at arm's length. The square adds stubbornness. You'd sooner understand the feeling than have it, and this card doesn't really allow for that.

Friendships are where it shows. You might pull back from the group, or throw yourself into it so there's never any time alone. With a partner it's needing space and then feeling lonely in it. Sleep can go odd, late nights reading about everything except the thing. Once, just once, let a friend see you upset without explaining it. Sit with them, say you're sad, and leave the reason out.
moon.reversed:
The cool head of an Aquarius Moon can go all the way to numb when this card is reversed. You've thought about the loss so much that it's turned into an idea. People might hear you talk about it almost in the third person. The square to Scorpio keeps you holding that stance long after it stopped helping. Every so often something small, a song in a shop, gets straight through, and you have no idea what to do with it.

With friends it shows as being there for every crisis except your own, and with a partner as a flatness they can't reach. Try doing something with your hands that's connected to what you lost, planting something, cooking their recipe, fixing the thing they left broken, and let whatever comes up come up.

rising.upright:
Friendly and slightly distant is how Aquarius rising usually comes across. You're interested in everyone and attached to no one, at least at first, and people often read you as unusual in a way they like. With the Five of Cups at the doorway, the distance is more noticeable. There's a reserve that wasn't there before, and a sense that part of your attention is somewhere else.

Aquarius and Scorpio are square, fixed air against fixed water, and that's friction that won't go away without some action. On the Ascendant it plays out as a front that's cooler than you mean it to be. Saturn rules your rising sign, and Mars there is a guest with Saturn's colouring, reserved and deliberate. Air and water don't mix easily, so strangers might sense something heavy and find no trace of it in what you say. Your instinct is to keep your own counsel. You'll talk cheerfully about anything else for hours.

At work people might find you brilliant and hard to reach, especially in a new team. With a new friend it's great conversation and no personal detail at all. On a date you'll be interesting and give nothing away. Let someone new ask you a personal question and answer it. Just the one, honestly, and see whether the rest of the evening feels different.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising keeps everyone at a very polite distance once this card turns upside down. You're friendly, you're interested, and nobody gets anywhere near you. People who've just met you find you a bit aloof, or a bit contrary, arguing a point for the sake of it. The fixed square locks the manner in, and it can take a long time to notice you're doing it.

At work it shows as independence tipping into isolation, turning down help and working alone. Socially it's joining a group and then keeping to the edge of it. With old friends it's going quiet in a way they find hard to read. Next time you're somewhere new, find the one person who looks as out of place as you and tell them why you almost didn't come.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns feel everything, their own and everyone else's, and this card is made almost entirely of feeling. Both signs are water, a trine apart, so the grief here doesn't knock at the door. It's already in the house. You understand this card without being told, and you probably understand the loss in ways nobody around you quite does.

Mars has no dignity in Pisces. It's a visitor there, softened by Jupiter and in the modern reading by Neptune, and it doesn't push very hard. That's the tension. The card is Mars in Scorpio, a feeling with force behind it, and in your sign the force dissolves. You feel the loss completely and struggle to act on it, to make the call or clear the room or say the thing. Mars also rules the last ten degrees of Pisces, where the card is the Ten of Cups, the family under the rainbow, so the same planet holds the far end of this suit in your sign.

It shows up in how much you absorb. A friend's break-up, a colleague's bad news, the news itself, all of it lands on top of your own. At work you might drift, doing the minimum and daydreaming. In love it can be longing for someone who isn't coming back, and finding the longing oddly comforting. Give your own grief a space apart from everyone else's. Write down whose sadness you've been carrying, and cross off everything that isn't yours.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun can drift into this card's grief and stay there when it's reversed. Sad songs, old messages, a haze where the loss turns into an atmosphere you live in. Or you escape it by whatever means is to hand, sleep, screens, a drink too many, someone else's drama. Mars is too diffuse here to push back, so there's nothing much to climb out with.

It shows in the body as tiredness and a foggy head, and in relationships as rescuing someone so you don't have to feel your own loss. At work you may be there in body and nowhere in mind. Pick one plain, practical thing connected to the loss, a form or a phone call or a box to sort, and finish it within a few days.

moon.upright:
Pisces Moons are porous. You pick up the mood of a room before you've taken your coat off, you cry at adverts, and you know a friend's upset from one text. Drop this card into that and it's water poured into water. Both are water signs, a trine apart, and nothing at all stands between you and the full weight of the feeling.

Mars in Pisces has no rank. It borrows Jupiter's largeness, and Neptune's fog in the modern reading, and the edges of the grief go soft. You may not be sure where your sadness ends and somebody else's begins. You might be sad about this loss and also, somehow, about every loss, the old ones and the ones you've only read about. The doubled water amplifies it, which cuts both ways. You let the feeling move through you and you'll cry freely, and that helps. It can also go on without edges for a long time.

Nights are where you'll notice it. Long heavy sleeps, or vivid dreams about the person or the place you lost. With a partner you'll want to be held and may find it hard to say what's wrong. With friends you might end up comforting them about your loss. Water helps you, quite literally. Take a long bath or go for a swim, and let yourself cry there, where it won't feel like too much.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, the grief of this card can spread through a Pisces Moon until it's the weather you live in. You're low, vaguely, all the time, and can't point to why. Or you escape it, into sleep, fantasy, a relationship that's mostly rescue. With Mars too soft here to cut a way out, drifting feels easiest.

It shows in the body as heaviness and too much sleep, and with other people as taking on their problems until you've no energy of your own left. Set a small boundary somewhere. Say no to one person's crisis, kindly, and use that hour for your own sadness, with a notebook or a long walk by the water.

rising.upright:
People tend to open up to Pisces rising within minutes. You meet the world softly, and strangers tell you things they'd normally keep for months. With this card drawn for your Ascendant, the softness has a sad edge. Some people will sense you've lost something and treat you gently. Others will just find you far away.

Both signs are water and they're trine, so the grief shows on your face without any effort. You can't really hide it, and to be honest you don't try very hard. Jupiter, which rules Pisces, is your chart ruler, and Mars in your rising sign has no dignity of its own and takes on Jupiter's colouring, generous and rather unfocused, which makes starting things difficult. Your instinct is to go with the current and see what happens, and this card's current runs sad. New people will bring you their own troubles too, because they can tell you'll understand.

At work you might seem a little absent, sympathetic to everyone and hard to pin down on anything. In a new relationship it's a tender openness that can attract people who want looking after. On a first date you'll be lovely and a bit melancholy. Choose one new situation and go in with a plan, a time to arrive, a time to leave, one thing you want from it, and stick to it.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising can lose its edges altogether under a reversed Five of Cups. You become whatever the person in front of you needs, the listener, the comforter, the fellow sufferer, and after a few weeks of that nobody's met you at all. The water's doubled and Mars can't hold a line here, so the boundary goes. Some days you come home from being around people and can't tell which feelings are yours.

At the office it's saying yes to everything and delivering vaguely. Socially it's drifting to the edge of the room, or into the arms of someone who needs rescuing. Next time you meet someone new, notice the moment you start mirroring them, their mood, their opinions, their sadness, and say one thing that's just yours.

1.upright:
Grief shows in the body before it shows anywhere else, and the first house is the body, the face, the way you walk into a room. It's an angular house, one of the chart's four corners, so what happens here gets seen. Its natural sign is Aries and its natural ruler is Mars, which puts this card's planet on its own ground. So the loss is on you, quite literally, in your posture and your energy and how you start the day.

The complication is the sign. The card is Mars in Scorpio, and Scorpio is five signs from Aries, a quincunx, with nothing much in common. Mars in the first house wants to push forward, and Mars in Scorpio wants to go down and stay down. The house is fire by nature and the card is water, and here it's the steam version. You may feel restless and heavy at once, desperate to get going and with no fuel to do it. People might tell you you look tired. You might catch your reflection and see the figure on the card, shoulders forward, head a bit low.

The body needs the most attention here. Sleep, food, and some kind of movement that isn't punishment, because Mars on home turf will happily turn its force on you. Your appearance might change without much thought, a haircut, weight up or down, a sudden habit of wearing black. In how you start things, the job applications or the new friendships, you'll be slower and more tentative. Look after the body as if it belonged to someone you loved, regular meals and a walk every day, and let the rest wait.
1.reversed:
The body tends to take the loss without it being named when this card is upside down in the first house. You're tense, run down, catching every cold going, and you put it down to being busy. Or you swing the other way and push the body hard, training, dieting, a whole new look, as though a different surface could fix what's underneath. Mars in its own house has plenty of force for that.

It shows in how you present yourself, a bit brittle, a bit too bright, and in how you start things, fast and then not at all. People close to you notice your face has changed. Once a day, stop and check in with your body the way you'd check a child who'd had a fall. Where does it hurt, what does it need, and can you give it that.

2.upright:
Money you can count and the worth you feel you have both live in the second house, and the two are tangled together far tighter than most people admit. It's a succedent house, the kind that builds up and holds on. This card in the second means something held has spilled. A job that paid, a sum you'd saved, an object that mattered, or the plain sense of being worth something, knocked by a rejection.

Taurus is the second house's natural sign, and Mars is in detriment there, working against the grain, so the card's way of dealing with loss runs against what this house wants. The second wants security and steadiness. The card wants to go down into the loss and feel it through. Scorpio and Taurus are opposites, the axis of what's mine and what's shared, and that often shows as money tied up with another person, a split, a debt, a joint account wound down. Earth and water do get on, though, and slowly things can grow back.

In the bank account it can be a real loss that needs grieving before it can be fixed, and that's worth doing honestly. In your sense of worth it might be a knock that makes you quote lower, ask for less, apologise for your prices. With possessions it can be the lost or broken thing you keep thinking about. Go through the actual numbers once, carefully, with a cup of tea and no judgement. Then write down three things you have that the loss didn't touch.
2.reversed:
Upside down in the second house, the card often turns a money loss into a habit. You keep paying for something that's finished, the subscription, the storage unit, the loan to a friend who isn't paying back. Or you clamp down so hard on spending that there's no pleasure left anywhere. Mars in detriment in the house's natural sign makes the stubbornness worse.

Self-worth takes the hit as well, quietly. You undercharge, you don't ask for the raise, you tell yourself you're lucky to have what you have. With a partner it can be a sore silence about who owes what. Pick one financial thing tied to the loss and close it off properly, a cancelled payment, a final message about the debt, a box of things sold or given away.

3.upright:
The third house covers the everyday traffic of your life. Messages, calls, the chat over the fence, the drive to the shops, your brothers and sisters, the things you're learning. Drawn here, the Five of Cups usually means a loss close to that everyday level. A falling-out with a sibling. A friendship that lived on daily texts and has gone quiet. A course you didn't finish, or a neighbourhood you had to leave.

Gemini gives this house its natural colour, and Gemini and Scorpio are a quincunx apart, five signs, with nothing in common. Air and water need introducing, and in this house they rarely get the chance. So the grief either gets talked about endlessly or not at all. It's a cadent house, the kind that processes and lets go, which is good news over time. For a while, though, you might find yourself going over the same conversation on every short trip, or drafting and deleting a message.

With a brother or sister, it may be a hurt that needs saying plainly and hasn't been. With neighbours or the local community, it can be the café that closed or the friend who moved away. In learning, it's the thing you've stopped studying because it reminds you of what went wrong. Write the message you've been avoiding, in three sentences, with no explanation longer than the apology. Send it or don't, as long as the words are out of your head.
3.reversed:
In the third house the reversed card can make words go sour. Small comments land harder than they should. You go over a message from your sister for an hour, reading the tone.
